request.raw_text: Add rounds to all edges of the part. R=0,2mm

areas_to_change.action: Apply constant-radius edge rounds (fillets) with radius 0.2 mm.
areas_to_change.reference_geometry: All topological edges of the existing solid part.
areas_to_change.location: Entire part, including the outer perimeter, bottom perimeter, end faces, side faces, flat end platforms, curved recessed surface boundaries, and all convex or concave face intersections.
areas_to_change.description: Replace every sharp edge with a tangent 0.2 mm radius transition while retaining the existing overall form.

areas_to_preserve.reference_geometry: Existing planar faces and the central curved recessed surface
areas_to_preserve.preservation_rule: Preserve their underlying geometry, orientation, and principal dimensions except for the narrow regions locally consumed by the rounds.

areas_to_preserve.reference_geometry: Overall rectangular footprint, part thickness, end platforms, and symmetric recessed profile
areas_to_preserve.preservation_rule: Maintain the current size, proportions, symmetry, and topology apart from the specified edge rounding.

predicted_final_outcome.geometry: The same saddle-like rectangular solid with every sharp edge replaced by a small, constant 0.2 mm radius fillet.
predicted_final_outcome.function: Reduce edge sharpness and provide a uniformly deburred, safer, and more manufacturable finish.
predicted_final_outcome.behavior: All adjacent surfaces transition smoothly and tangentially across the rounded edge bands; the small radius causes negligible change to the overall envelope and supporting profile.

ambiguities.description: The decimal comma in "R=0,2mm" is interpreted as a metric radius of 0.2 mm.
candidate_interpretations: If the comma is not intended as a decimal separator, the radius value requires clarification.

ambiguities.description: "All edges" may include every modeled topological edge, including concave edges and edges that are not normally treated as exposed exterior edges.
candidate_interpretations: Apply 0.2 mm rounds to every geometrically feasible edge of the solid.
Apply 0.2 mm rounds only to exposed sharp exterior edges.
